brief: GS's Oct 23 flow note: S&P fell 121bps to 7663 (Nasdaq -2.9%) in an AI risk-off move after Meta's earnings, hitting Lam (-13%), Ciena (-11%) and Meta (-7%) while Meta's CDS widened; GS's AI basket is now -23% since June and SOX underperformed the S&P by 13% over 9 sessions, its worst stretch in 20+ years, now testing its 200dma. A WSJ finding of roughly $3tr in AI-related off-balance-sheet commitments, including $1.2tr in leases, plus an S&P Global warning on interconnected AI financing, add a debt-cost dimension to the selloff. Yet GS's US team still likes the broadening trade: SPXXAI outperformed SPX by 6% in October and the AI/SPXXAI correlation is reverting lower, with defensive sectors (Staples +3%, Healthcare +2%) rotating higher. GS prime-brokerage data showed Fundamental L/S, Systematics and Multi-Strats all down more than 1% for the first time since Covid, 155 S&P names made 2-sigma moves (most since the May 2025 tariff truce), and Unconstrained Momentum is having its worst drawdown since the GFC. Separately, GS raised its Meta price target to $885 from $860 on Muse monetization strength.
